Compute the bending normal stress at a single cross-section of a rectangular beam using the flexure formula sigma = M * y / I.
The applied bending moment at the section is M = 4,000,000 N·mm, positive sign convention means the bottom fiber is in tension and the top fiber is in compression.
The cross-section is rectangular with width b = 50 mm and overall height h = 120 mm.
The coordinate y is measured from the neutral axis (centroid of the section) upward as positive, so the top fiber is at y = +60 mm and the bottom fiber is at y = -60 mm.
The second moment of area for the rectangular section is I = b * h^3 / 12, which evaluates to 50 * 120^3 / 12 = 7,200,000 mm^4.
Report the bending normal stress at three specific fiber locations: y = 0 mm (neutral axis), y = +60 mm (top fiber), and y = -60 mm (bottom fiber).
All quantities use the N–mm–MPa unit system throughout; no unit conversion is required.
State the governing relation sigma = M * y / I explicitly in the output.
Note that at y = 0 the bending stress is zero by the flexure formula, confirming the neutral-axis definition.
At the top fiber (y = +60 mm) the computed stress will be negative, indicating compression.
At the bottom fiber (y = -60 mm) the computed stress will be positive, indicating tension.
Assume small deformation and linear elastic material behavior consistent with Euler-Bernoulli beam theory; shear deformation, stress concentrations, and nonlinear material effects are neglected.
